frontmatter.subject: the ways a statement can function, and the relationships among them
frontmatter.normative: scope, categories, criterion, objects, relationships, composition, refusals, subsumptions, invariants, boundary, owed

scope.models: The closed set of ways a statement can function, the relationships among those ways, and the structures they form. A way a statement can function is called a kind. The objects section states the kinds and the relationships section states the relationships.
scope.abstraction: This model is independent of implementation, protocol, and encoding. No normative claim here holds only if a storage form, a serialization, a key, an identifier scheme, a query language, a protocol, or a product is a particular one.

excludes.subject: What exists in a domain: which referents there are, which predicates the domain admits, and what each predicate may take.
How a statement is carried, how it is identified, how a kind is fixed to it, and how it is admitted.
Storage, encoding, order, indexing, transport, and evaluation.
excludes.owner: Any realization, bounded by the boundary section.

primitives.assumed: A statement is something said. It has exactly three positions: subject, predicate, value.

A referent is what a position holds when what it holds is a thing rather than a value, a statement, or a kind. Whether two referents are one referent is determinate. This model does not decide it, never names a referent, and never describes one.

A literal is what a position holds when what it holds is identical to itself in every set of statements with no correspondence asserted. Two literals are one literal when they are equal. This model states no vocabulary of literals and admits no division of them into sorts.
A coordinate is a literal on the one time axis. Coordinates are totally ordered. This model states one time axis and no other.

A position holds a referent, a literal, a statement, a kind of this model, or nothing. A position holding nothing is unbound. Whether a position is bound is determinate, and which of the four a bound position holds is determinate.

category.name: first-order
category.recognition-rule: Every bound position holds a referent or a literal.

boundary-example.inside: A subscription began at a coordinate. Subject and predicate hold referents, value holds a literal.
boundary-example.outside: Someone put that statement forward. Its subject holds a statement, so it is second-order.

category.name: second-order
category.recognition-rule: At least one position holds a statement, and none holds a kind.

boundary-example.inside: An artifact bears a statement. The subject holds a statement.
boundary-example.outside: An artifact was produced at a coordinate. It holds referents and a literal, so it is first-order.

category.name: reflexive
category.recognition-rule: At least one position holds a kind of this model.

boundary-example.inside: A domain predicate specializes a kind this model states.
boundary-example.outside: One domain predicate specializes another. Both positions hold referents, so it is first-order.

categories.exhaustive: Every candidate falls in exactly one category. Occupancy is exhaustively referent, literal, statement, kind, or unbound, and the primitives section makes which one determinate. A kind in any position decides reflexive; a statement with no kind decides second-order; otherwise first-order.

term.name: candidate
term.definition: A proposed kind, offered for admission to the objects section. Never a particular statement.

term.name: position
term.definition: One of the three places in a statement: subject, predicate, value.

criterion.procedure: The recognition rules in the categories section are the procedure. They are mutually exclusive, so no ordering among them binds.

step.test: Which recognition rule in the categories section does the candidate satisfy?

criterion.terminal-outcome: A candidate satisfying no recognition rule is not a way a statement functions. It is a referent, which this model does not name, a literal, which this model does not divide, or a vocabulary, which the pack model closes.

objects.declaration-order: Significant. Declaration order is the order of the kinds wherever an order over kinds is required, and the sequence below fixes it.

object.name: entity

property.name: subject
property.value-space: One referent.

property.name: predicate
property.value-space: One referent whose concept specializes entity.

property.name: value
property.value-space: One referent, or unbound.

object.formation-rule: Premises: the subject holds a referent; the predicate's concept specializes entity. Conclusion: the statement functions as entity.
object.refuses: Asserting what class the subject belongs to. That is concept.

object.name: event

property.name: subject
property.value-space: One referent.

property.name: predicate
property.value-space: One referent whose concept specializes event.

property.name: value
property.value-space: One referent, one literal, or unbound.

object.formation-rule: Premises: the subject holds a referent; the predicate's concept specializes event. Conclusion: the statement functions as event.
object.refuses: Asserting what obtains across an interval. That is state under a context.

object.name: state

property.name: subject
property.value-space: One referent.

property.name: predicate
property.value-space: One referent whose concept specializes state.

property.name: value
property.value-space: One referent or one literal.

object.formation-rule: Premises: the subject holds a referent; the predicate's concept specializes state; the value is bound. Conclusion: the statement functions as state.
object.refuses: Carrying when it obtains, and whether it still obtains. When is a context over it; whether is the held judgment.

object.name: role

property.name: subject
property.value-space: One referent.

property.name: predicate
property.value-space: One referent whose concept specializes role.

property.name: value
property.value-space: One referent naming the capacity.

object.formation-rule: Premises: the subject holds a referent; the predicate's concept specializes role; the value holds a referent. Conclusion: the statement functions as role.
object.refuses: Being a property of the subject. One referent holds several capacities and remains one referent.

object.name: relation

property.name: subject
property.value-space: One referent, or one statement.

property.name: predicate
property.value-space: One referent whose concept specializes relation.

property.name: value
property.value-space: One referent, or one statement.

object.formation-rule: Premises: the predicate's concept specializes relation; subject and value are both bound. Conclusion: the statement functions as relation.
object.refuses: Carrying when the connection began or whether it still holds.

object.name: claim

property.name: subject
property.value-space: One statement.

property.name: predicate
property.value-space: One referent whose concept specializes claim.

property.name: value
property.value-space: One referent naming who put the subject forward.

object.formation-rule: Premises: the subject holds a statement; the predicate's concept specializes claim. Conclusion: the statement functions as claim.
object.refuses: Settling the subject. Assertion is a ground, not a verdict.

object.name: evidence

property.name: subject
property.value-space: One statement.

property.name: predicate
property.value-space: One referent whose concept specializes evidence.

property.name: value
property.value-space: One referent naming what bears the subject.

object.formation-rule: Premises: the subject holds a statement; the predicate's concept specializes evidence. Conclusion: the statement functions as evidence.

object.name: derivation

property.name: subject
property.value-space: One statement, bound.

property.name: predicate
property.value-space: One referent whose concept specializes derivation.

property.name: value
property.value-space: One statement functioning as rule.

object.formation-rule: Premises: the subject holds a bound statement; the predicate's concept specializes derivation; the value holds a statement functioning as rule; the subject is that rule's conclusion under a binding of the rule's unbound positions. Conclusion: the statement functions as derivation.
object.refuses: Asserting that the subject currently holds. The held judgment computes that.

object.name: invalidation

property.name: subject
property.value-space: One statement.

property.name: predicate
property.value-space: One referent whose concept specializes invalidation.

property.name: value
property.value-space: One referent naming who released the subject.

object.formation-rule: Premises: the subject holds a statement; the predicate's concept specializes invalidation. Conclusion: the statement functions as invalidation.
object.refuses: Removing the subject. The released statement remains and remains reachable.

object.name: rule

property.name: subject
property.value-space: One statement carrying one or more unbound positions.

property.name: predicate
property.value-space: One referent whose concept specializes rule.

property.name: value
property.value-space: One statement whose unbound positions appear in the subject.

object.formation-rule: Premises: the subject holds a statement carrying unbound positions; the predicate's concept specializes rule; every unbound position of the value appears in the subject. Conclusion: the statement functions as rule.
object.refuses: Naming any predicate belonging to a domain. A rule reaches a domain through concept.

object.name: context

property.name: subject
property.value-space: One statement.

property.name: predicate
property.value-space: One referent whose concept specializes context.

property.name: value
property.value-space: One referent or one literal bounding where or when the subject is put forward.

object.formation-rule: Premises: the subject holds a statement; the predicate's concept specializes context. Conclusion: the statement functions as context.
object.refuses: Ranking scopes against one another. Which scope binds a question is decided by the question.

object.name: concept

property.name: subject
property.value-space: One referent.

property.name: predicate
property.value-space: One referent whose concept specializes concept.

property.name: value
property.value-space: One kind of this model, or one referent held in the subject position of another statement functioning as concept.

object.formation-rule: Premises: the subject holds a referent; the predicate's concept specializes concept, and the statement itself satisfies that premise when its subject and its predicate are one referent; the value holds a kind of this model or a referent classified by another concept. Conclusion: the statement functions as concept.
object.refuses: Naming what exists. A concept classifies a referent and this model classifies none.

relationship.name: concerns

participant.object: any kind with a position holding a referent

relationship.direction: Directed from the statement to the referent.
relationship.constraint: Every statement stands in this relationship at its predicate position.
relationship.refuses: Holding a literal, a statement, or a kind.

relationship.name: carries

participant.object: any kind with a position holding a literal

relationship.direction: Directed from the statement to the literal.
relationship.constraint: A literal has no positions and stands as holder in no relationship.
relationship.refuses: Holding a referent, a statement, or a kind.

relationship.name: about

participant.object: any kind with a position holding a statement

relationship.direction: Directed from the holding statement to the held statement.
relationship.constraint: The held statement may itself stand as holder. Composition is unbounded.
Acyclic. No statement reaches itself by following this relationship.
relationship.refuses: Holding a referent, a literal, or a kind.

relationship.name: specializes

participant.object: any kind with a position holding a kind of this model

relationship.direction: Directed from the specializing concept to the kind it specializes.
relationship.constraint: One step. A kind of this model stands as held only, never as holder.
relationship.refuses: Holding a referent, a literal, or a statement. A concept whose value holds a referent stands in concerns, and the classification judgment carries it to a kind.

relationships.closed: Closed at four. A relationship constrains exactly one occupancy. The primitives section admits five, of which unbound is the absence of one, leaving referent, literal, statement, kind. Concerns constrains the first, carries the second, about the third, specializes the fourth. A fifth relationship would constrain an occupancy the primitives do not admit. A constraint on which kind occupies a position, as derivation's value requires, is stated by that property and is not a relationship, because the occupancy remains a statement.

judgment.name: classification
judgment.form: p ↑ K, read as predicate referent p reaches kind K.
judgment.premise: Some statement C functioning as concept holds p in its subject position and K in its value position.

judgment.name: classification, transitive
judgment.premise: Some C functioning as concept holds p in its subject position and q in its value position, and q ↑ K.

judgment.name: kind assignment
judgment.form: S : K, read as statement S functions as kind K.
judgment.premise: S's predicate position holds p, and p ↑ K.
S satisfies the formation rule of K.

judgment.name: kind assignment, base
judgment.premise: S's subject position and S's predicate position hold one referent.
S's value position holds the kind concept.

judgment.name: classification, well-founded
judgment.premise: Following classification from p reaches a statement satisfying kind assignment, base, in finitely many steps.
judgment.conclusion: The chain from p is finite and reaches a kind of this model.

judgment.name: bound
judgment.premise: No position of S is unbound.

judgment.name: same
judgment.premise: For each of the three positions, the occupants in S and T are one referent, are equal literals, are one kind, satisfy this judgment recursively, or are both unbound.

judgment.name: grounded
judgment.premise: Some W in G holds a statement T in its subject position with S ≡ T, and W : claim, or W : evidence, or W : derivation.

judgment.name: held
judgment.premise: No V in G with V : invalidation holds a statement T in its subject position with S ≡ T.

judgment.name: held at
judgment.premise: The subset of G whose members are confined by a context whose value is a coordinate at or before c grounds S and releases it in no invalidation.

composition.well-formed: A statement is well-formed when S : K holds for exactly one K and each of its three positions is occupied as K's value-spaces state. A set is well-formed when every member is well-formed, every statement occupying a position of a member is itself a member, and every predicate in the set reaches a kind.
composition.underivable: No derivation exists for: a statement whose predicate reaches two kinds; a statement whose predicate reaches none; a statement satisfying the formation rule of a kind its predicate does not reach; a derivation whose subject carries an unbound position; a rule whose value carries an unbound position absent from its subject; a predicate whose classification chain reaches no kind, revisits a referent, or reaches no base case; a set in which a statement reaches itself through the about relationship; grounded or held over a statement that is not bound.
composition.dynamics: This model defines no evaluation, no reduction, and no operation other than formation. None of the judgments rewrites a statement and none produces one.

refusal.candidate: Any kind of thing: a classification naming what exists.
refusal.ground: A kind naming what exists makes this model a vocabulary. A vocabulary must be adopted. Two sets of statements whose authors disagree about what exists then share no term.
refusal.lost: This model says nothing about any subject matter. A domain reaches it only through concept.

refusal.ground: A predicate is a referent a domain names. Naming one here makes this model a vocabulary, on the ground above.
refusal.lost: This model states no predicate, and every statement's predicate comes from a domain.

refusal.candidate: A kind asserting the current standing of a statement.
refusal.ground: The held judgment computes standing. A kind asserting it gives one question two answers that disagree.
refusal.lost: Standing is computed and never asserted.

refusal.candidate: A kind asserting a degree of confidence, probability, or similarity.
refusal.ground: The grounded judgment admits three grounds and none is a magnitude.
refusal.lost: Degree grounds nothing. A magnitude asserted about a statement is a claim whose subject is a state.

refusal.candidate: A division of literals into sorts.
refusal.ground: Which sorts exist is chosen, and a chosen member set here is a vocabulary.
refusal.lost: This model states no arithmetic and no comparison over literals other than equality and the total order on coordinates.

subsumption.candidate: validity, the time a statement holds over
subsumption.expression: A context whose value is a coordinate bounds when the subject is put forward. Two contexts bound both ends.
An invalidation releasing the earlier statement and a separate statement asserting the replacement.
A report is a claim whose value names the observer. A recording is a referent, and evidence cites it.
Which of the three grounding kinds holds a statement in its subject position.
A role asserts a capacity. A rule takes roles among its premises and concludes what is permitted.
That two referents are one is a relation, and asserting it is a claim, groundable and releasable.
A statement put forward and grounded no other way is a claim.
A version is the set satisfying the held at judgment for one coordinate.
When something obtains is a context on the first-order statement. When it was put forward is a context on the claim or derivation standing to it. One axis carries both.
A relation whose subject is the derivation and whose value is an input statement. One per input.

invariant.claim: No kind names anything belonging to any domain.
invariant.refuter: A value-space, formation rule, or refuses line satisfiable in one domain and not another.

invariant.claim: Every statement has exactly three positions.
invariant.refuter: An object stating a fourth property, or fewer than three.

invariant.claim: Every statement's kind is the kind its predicate reaches.
invariant.refuter: A formation rule assigning a kind without consulting the predicate's classification.

invariant.claim: Concept is the only kind with a position holding a kind of this model.
invariant.refuter: A second kind whose value-space admits a kind.

invariant.claim: Every relationship constrains exactly one occupancy the primitives admit, and every admitted occupancy other than unbound is constrained by exactly one relationship.
invariant.refuter: A relationship constraining two, two constraining one, or an admitted occupancy none constrains.

invariant.claim: No normative claim holds only if a storage form, serialization, identifier scheme, protocol, query language, or product is a particular one.
invariant.refuter: A normative claim whose truth changes when any of those is exchanged.

invariant.claim: Every judgment premise is decided by inspecting position occupancy, the primitives declared in the scope section, the objects section, and the relationships section.
invariant.refuter: A premise requiring knowledge of how something is stored, encoded, transported, or evaluated.

invariant.claim: The classification chain from every predicate is finite and terminates in a kind of this model.
invariant.refuter: A concept admitted with no path to the base case, or a chain that revisits a referent.

boundary.realization-class: Many realizations derive from this model. A realization is anything that carries statements and assigns kinds to them. No realization is privileged.

must-supply.obligation: A carrier for a statement with three positions: subject, predicate, value.
Exactly one kind per statement, taken from the kind its predicate reaches and not chosen by whoever writes the statement.
The kinds as declared, under the declared order, with none added and none omitted.
The occupancies as distinguished here, so that a position holding a referent is distinguishable from one holding a literal.
A means of occupying a position with a statement, and of detecting a cycle through the about relationship.
A means of leaving a position unbound and of binding it, so that rule and derivation are distinguishable.
One time axis, totally ordered, carrying every coordinate.
Standing computed by the held judgment, never asserted and never stored.
A means of classifying a domain predicate through concept, such that every predicate reaches a kind.
One referent satisfying the base case of kind assignment, standing as its own predicate, so that the classification chain terminates.

boundary.may-choose: How a statement is carried, encoded, ordered, indexed, transported, or addressed.
What the three positions are called in its own surface.
Which literals it admits, and how it writes them.
Whether it evaluates rules to derivations, and by what strategy.
boundary.may-not-decide: That a statement has three positions.
Which relationships exist, or what occupancy each constrains.
How a statement acquires its kind.
The declaration order of the kinds.
Whether standing is computed or stored.
How many time axes there are.
Whether two statements are one statement.
boundary.direction: Every obligation runs from this model to a realization. No claim in a normative section holds only if a realization chooses a particular way.

item.fact: This section carries no item. Every fact settled here that another document must carry is named in the scope section with its owner.
